date_note: Edaily reports the explanatory session held on the 25th; the page gives no earlier day.
exec: Per Edaily, South Korea's amended network act requires firms to appoint a CISO as an executive and notify users of breaches.
org: Ministry of Science and ICT (South Korea)
plain: South Korea's science ministry explained amended rules to industry: companies must name a CISO as an executive, notify affected users of breaches, and may be fined for repeated breaches.
summary: Edaily reports that the Ministry of Science and ICT and KISA held an explanatory session in Seoul on the 25th on the amended Information and Communications Network Act and its Enforcement Decree. According to the article, companies must designate a CISO as an executive, notify affected users of breaches, and can face fines if breached repeatedly.
title: South Korea's science ministry briefs industry on amended network act: executive CISO, user notification, fines for repeated breaches

validation.note: Single publisher (Edaily) reporting the ministry's own session; ministry page not read.
